newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Court ruling another blow for Colombia's Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Court ruling another blow for Colombia's Telecom.

text.p: For the second time this week, a top court has ruled that Colombia's state-run Empresa Colombia de Telecomunicaciones (Telecom) has no business monopolizing long distance telephone service.
The latest ruling, following a similar one in the capital Tuesday, was handed down by the Superior Court in the northwest city of Medellin, court sources said.

They said the ruling effectively authorized Empresas Publicas de Medellin (EPM), the country's largest utility, to start competing with Telecom by providing long distance telephone service in the metropolitan area of Medellin later this year.
The court gave the government's Telecommunications Regulatory Commission 60 days to set the terms under which EPM will be able to enter into the long distance market.

But Mauricio Restrepo, EPM's general manager, said he was certain that there would be no restrictions. "With this ruling, the country wins and businesses win because it puts us on an equal footing with Telecom," Restrepo said.
Tuesday's ruling in Bogota authorized the city's Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Santa Fe de Bogota to start providing national and international long distance service.
